problems.title: Rewrite the numerator around its denominator
problems.question: Find (x+67y)/(x+y) if (x+y)/y=1/3.
steps: The given reciprocal is y/(x+y)=3.
Thus the value is 1+66·3=199. The given fractions ensure the denominators are nonzero.

problems.title: Order five products from intervals
problems.question: -2<a<-1<b<0<1<c<2<d. Order ab,ac,ad,bc,cd.
problems.idea: Separate negative from positive products first.
formulas: a<0 and d>c>0 imply ad<ac; a<b and c>0 imply ac<bc.
steps: The products ad,ac,bc are negative, while ab,cd are positive.
Because |a|<2 and |b|<1, 0<ab<2. Since c>1,d>2, cd>2.
Combine both chains.

problems.title: A zero sum of absolute values
problems.question: Solve |(x-y)(5x-4y)|+|4x-3y-1|=0.
problems.idea: Both absolute values must be zero.
steps: If x=y, the linear equation gives x=y=1.
If 5x=4y, then y=5x/4 and 4x-15x/4=1, giving x=4,y=5.
Both pairs satisfy the original equation.

problems.title: Compare road and sea journey lengths
problems.question: A road route is 76 km longer than the sea route. A car takes 4 hours outward and a ship 2 hours back. The car is 25% slower than the ship. Find the road length.
problems.idea: Let the ship speed be v.
steps: Their difference is v=76.
The road length is 3·76=228.

problems.title: A sum of cubes exposes a shared factor
problems.question: Factor 3x³+7x²+14xy+24y³.
problems.idea: Group the cubic terms and the two middle terms.
steps: Write the expression as 3(x³+8y³)+7x(x+2y).
Extract x+2y from both parts.

problems.title: Integer quotient from a polynomial remainder
problems.question: Find all integers n making (n³+9n²+6n+31)/(n+1) an integer.
problems.idea: Divide by n+1 and retain its nonzero restriction.
steps: Thus n+1 must be a positive or negative divisor of 33.
The possible divisors are ±1,±3,±11,±33.
Subtract 1 from each.

problems.title: Reflect the orthocenter in a side
problems.question: ABC has angles 50°,60°,70° and orthocenter H. The B-altitude meets AC at B₁ and the circumcircle again at K. Given KB₁=12, find HB₁.
problems.idea: The reflection of the orthocenter across a side lies on the circumcircle.
formulas: Reflection across AC preserves B₁ and reverses the perpendicular altitude line.
steps: To see the circle property, the reflected point H′ has AH′C=180°-B, so A,B,C,H′ are cyclic.
Because H′ is on the line BH, it is the second circle intersection K.
B₁ is therefore the midpoint of HK, giving HB₁=KB₁=12.

problems.title: Altitude-bisector deviation from angle ratios
problems.question: A:B:C=1:3:8. CH is an altitude and CL the C-bisector. Find HCL.
problems.idea: The angle between these two lines is half |A-B|.
steps: The unit is 15°, so A=15°,B=45°,C=120°.

problems.title: Two perpendicular bisectors through the same midpoint
problems.question: In right ABC with right vertex C, M is the hypotenuse midpoint. O,I are circumcentres of ACM,BCM. Prove IMO=90°.
problems.idea: M is equally far from all three original vertices.
formulas: MA=MB=MC; the locus equidistant from two points is their perpendicular bisector.
steps: Both O and M are equidistant from A,C, so OM is perpendicular to AC.
Both I and M are equidistant from B,C, so IM is perpendicular to BC.
Since AC⊥BC, their perpendicular lines OM,IM are also perpendicular.

problems.title: An angle bisector and a tangent form an isosceles triangle
problems.question: AD bisects A in triangle ABC. The circumcircle tangent at A meets ray BC at E. Prove EAD is isosceles.
problems.idea: Use the tangent-chord theorem and the bisected angle.
formulas: Tangent-chord angle equals the inscribed angle in the opposite segment.
steps: As E lies outside the circle on ray BC, it lies beyond C. Thus EAB=180°-C by the tangent-chord theorem.
Then EAD=180°-C-A/2.
In triangle ADC, ADE=ADC=180°-C-A/2 because DE follows DC.
The equal angles at A,D imply EA=ED.
problems.note: The statement assumes the tangent actually meets ray BC. In the isosceles case AB=AC the tangent is parallel to BC, so that intersection does not exist.
